newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asian crudes; Oman premium rises, eyes on Bangchak.
newsitem.headline: Asian crudes; Oman premium rises, eyes on Bangchak.

text.p: Oman's premium climbed slightly on Thursday as overall values for crudes fell in line with the weakness seen in global futures prices.
Another flurry of Oman trades -- the last main remaining market for December Gulf grades -- saw the premium climb to 10.5 cents above MPM.
The deal was confirmed between a Japanese trader and a Japanese refiner for 500,000 barrels.
Another Japanese trader sold a cargo of Oman to China at MPM +10 cents and a European trader sold a cargo to China at MPM +9.5 cents.
Minas firmed slightly, traders said, with a major selling 250,000 barrels to Australia at a premium of 33 cents, traders said. The deal was not immediately confirmed.
In the light sweet market, prices were firming.
A European trader sold a U.S. major a cargo of December Dulang at APPI Tapis quotes plus 70 cents, while a December Cossack changed hands within Australia at Tapis quotes plus 35 cents.
The previous high premium for Oman barrels was +10 cents.
Traders said other Oman cargos traded at slightly lower levels, with a European major, which is usually a seller, a noted buyer.
The focus now shifts to the Bangchak tender for December crude. Up to eight cargos of Oman have been offered at MPM plus six to 12 cents, industry sources said.
The tender also sought Far East light sweet crude and the sources said two December Tapis were offered at benchmark quotes plus $1.50 to $1.60.
A November cargo was offered at quotes plus $1.40.
